title: Mugwort and the Tiny Light
markdown:
In the rocky peaks the wind sang old songs and the stars sat like scattered jewellery. Mugwort the young ogre was not the sort who scared towns. Kind, heart as large as his feet, steps that shook mountain, laugh like happy boulders. He wanted a friend who would not leap at his Good morning or his heavy sighs. Size and boom, he feared, were a kind of weather little creatures fled.

Pip the panda, moss-soft, nudged a big hand. “A pet is a quest. Your greetings are a bit… lively.” Luna Bright, goat, horns catching starlight, danced around tree-trunk boots. “He waved at a field mouse and it changed counties. Shy things come out when the world is quiet. Look under the moon. It makes everything gentler.”

The moon climbed, a silver coin, slopes in pearl. They left the cozy place. Woods went hush. Every rustle, every careful twig, drummed Mugwort’s chest. Mice under ferns: “Hello, little friends!” Boom. Vanished. A badger into a den. His whisper was still a strong wind. Birds left the pines.

Then, among sighing trees, a dragon not of fire but of light: scales every jewel, preening at a clear pool, neck a graceful question. Voice like wind chimes. “Lovely moonlight. Divine on my emerald. Perfect.”

Mugwort stepped to admire. A hidden root. Wobble, groan, arms, pinecones raining. One found the splendid head.

“Clumsy! Mussed my finest scale. Ages to smooth.” Iridescent claw, pinecone dismissed.

Ears drooped. “Terribly sorry. I wanted to approach gently.”

The dragon huffed, checked the pool, softened a fraction. “Your apology is almost as grand as you. The forest floor is not a bouncing castle.” Back to the reflection.

Mugwort trudged to a brook that sang sad over stones. “Too big. Too loud. Kind heart, awkward body.”

A tiny light blinked in the twilight: Flicker, a glow-worm no bigger than a thumb, who had watched from mossy roots without fear. Admiration, quiet. He wriggled closer, warmth steady.

“You sound sad.”

Mugwort descended, breath a puff. “You aren’t scared?”

“You look sad, not scary. Your heart sounds kind. Your voice is only distant thunder.”

A real smile, craggy and wide. Pip and Luna understood without speeches. One enormous fingertip. Flicker climbed, as if the fingertip had always been a path. Mugwort held still, jewel-careful.

“My own,” he whispered, breeze not rumble. Pip purred. Luna nudged a knee. They did not explain kindness. Under the moon the ogre who had feared his own weather walked home with a light on his finger that had chosen him on purpose.
characters: Mugwort (Mugwort the young ogre), Pip (mountain companions)
author: StoryGen Community
